title: Communication Tactics (Questions and Listening)
description: Using questions, active listening, and strategic silence to gather information, build rapport, and uncover what the other side truly values.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Using questions, active listening, and strategic silence to gather information, build rapport, and uncover what the other side truly values.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: Instead of arguing, a skilled negotiator asks: 'Help me understand why that number is important to you.'
After an offer, they stay silent. The other side fills the silence with concessions or additional information.
They summarize: 'So if I'm hearing you correctly, delivery speed matters more than a small price difference. Is that right?'

sections.title: Real-World Phrases
content: What would make this a great deal for you, aside from price?
I noticed you hesitated when I mentioned the timeline. Can you tell me more?
Let me summarize what I'm hearing to make sure I understand.

sections.title: Common Mistake
sections.content: Talking more than listening. In effective negotiations, the ratio of listening to speaking is often 2:1 or higher.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: The person asking questions controls the direction. The person listening controls the information.
